item.title: Joe Alt, Derwin James remain out of practice for Chargers
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Chargers remained without a few starters at Thursday's practice.
item.content:encoded:
The Chargers remained without a few starters at Thursday's practice.

Right tackle Joe Alt (neck), left guard Kayode Awosika, cornerback Donte Jackson (hamstring), and safety Derwin James (hamstring) were all out of practice for the second time this week. All four players missed Week 5 and the status quo with their participation suggests they're on track to miss another game when the Chargers face the Chiefs this Sunday.

Linebacker Bud Dupree (neck, rest) and cornerback Rodney Shelley (hamstring) were out after being limited on Wednesday.

Defensive lineman Jamaree Caldwell (knee), defensive lineman Justin Eboige (shoulder), linebacker Daiyan Henley (shoulder), wide receiver Quentin Johnston (chest), wide receiver KeAndre Lambert-Smith (hamstring), wide receiver Ladd McConkey (foot), defensive back Elijah Molden (hamstring), wide receiver Brenen Thompson (quad), defensive lineman Dalvin Tomlinson (hamstring), and safety Kendall Williamson (ankle) were all limited participants.

Tight end Charlie Kolar (forearm), linebacker Khalil Mack (rest), and wide receiver Marquez Valdes-Scantling (rib) were full participants.

item.title: Sam Darnold: Unfair to our team that I keep turning the ball over, I have to be better
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: "No way to sugarcoat it: That one sucked. Can't turn the ball over," Darnold said.
item.content:encoded:
Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold was blunt in his self-assessment after Thursday night's loss to the Broncos.

"No way to sugarcoat it: That one sucked. Can't turn the ball over," Darnold said immediately upon taking the podium at his post-game press conference.

Darnold threw two interceptions, one in the fourth quarter and one in overtime, of a game the Seahawks would ultimately lose 17-14. He acknowledged afterward that the defense and special teams played well enough to win, and he did not.

"When you have a defense and special teams group that's playing the way they are for us, for me, I've just got to protect the football," Darnold said. "Dropping back and taking what they give me, I feel like I did a pretty good job of that in the first half, and then late in the second half, those two plays, you can't have it."

Darnold knows that the loss was on him.

"It's BS for me to keep turning the ball over," Darnold said. "It's not fair to our defense. It's not fair to our special teams. It's not fair to our entire team. I've got to be better."

item.content:encoded:
The Eagles announced on Thursday that quarterback Jalen Hurts will not play against the Panthers due to a blood clot in his calf, which leaves Tanner McKee in line to make the first non-Week 18 start of his career.

McKee may have wide receiver DeVonta Smith available for the game. Smith has missed the last two games with a hamstring injury and he did not practice on Wednesday, but the team listed him as a limited participant in Thursday's practice.

Wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks is moving in the opposite direction with his hamstring injury. Wicks was out of practice Thursday after working on a limited basis on Wednesday.

Running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring) remained out of practice and is on track to miss his second straight game. Defensive back Michael Carter (abdomen), linebacker AJ Epenesa (back), linebacker Jalyx Hunt (knee, ankle), and running back Will Shipley (foot) were also out on Thursday.

item.title: Colts release WR Darius Slayton
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: The Darius Slayton experiment in Indianapolis has come to an end.
item.content:encoded:
The Darius Slayton experiment in Indianapolis has come to an end.

The Colts announced on Friday that the team has released Slayton, ending the veteran wideout’s short stint with the club.

Indianapolis had signed Slayton after Alec Pierce went down early in the season with the hope that he could fill in as a deep threat.

But nearly a month later, Slatyon had yet to see the field. Now, the Colts have moved on.

Last season, Slayton caught 37 passes for 538 yards with one touchdown in 14 games for the Giants last year.

item.title: Bo Nix: I don't know where the disconnect is offensively
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The point of playing football games is to win football games and the Broncos were able to do that against the Seahawks on Thursday night, but the result didn't shield their quarterback Bo Nix from some harsh criticism after the game.
item.content:encoded:
The point of playing football games is to win football games and the Broncos were able to do that against the Seahawks on Thursday night, but the result didn't shield their quarterback Bo Nix from some harsh criticism after the game.

During the Prime Video postgame show, former NFL quarterback Ryan Fitzpatrick called Nix's performance in the 17-14 overtime victory "garbage." The Broncos picked up 153 yards on a pair of early touchdown drives that staked them to a 14-0 lead, but they only picked up two first downs over the rest of the night while punting seven times and the futility allowed the Seahawks to send the game to overtime.

Nix finished 17-of-27 for 107 yards and the team's longest pass play went for 16 yards, which he said after the game was not part of a design to be overly conservative and that he doesn't "understand why we can’t really push the ball vertically right now." Nix said he recognizes the need to do that for the offense to pull equal weight to the defense in Denver.

“We’re definitely capable," Nix said. "We’ve shown it and I don’t where the disconnect is right now to be honest with you. . . . I just think we're really, for some reason, struggling to find those explosive plays and that’s what makes an offense really spectacular — finding explosive plays. And right now we don’t have those.”

The one positive that Nix could point to is that the Broncos did not turn the ball over while the Seahawks gave it away three times, including an overtime interception that set up Denver's winning points. Head coach Sean Payton didn't delve into the offense's struggles beyond saying "we’re going to see a lot that we want to clean up," but it is clear that his decision to take over playcalling has not solved all that's wrong with Nix or the rest of the unit.

item.title: Tanner McKee: I'm ready to make the most of "huge opportunity"
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Tanner McKee fell to No. 3 on the depth chart ahead of Week 1 this season, but he worked his way back to the No. 2 job in time to be the next man up when the Eagles made a surprising announcement on Thursday.
item.content:encoded:
Tanner McKee fell to No. 3 on the depth chart ahead of Week 1 this season, but he worked his way back to the No. 2 job in time to be the next man up when the Eagles made a surprising announcement on Thursday.

Jalen Hurts will not play against the Panthers in Week 6 because of a blood clot in his calf and it is unclear when he will be cleared to return to action. That positions the 2023 sixth-round pick to make his first start outside of a pair of throwaway Week 18 games after the Eagles had already clinched their postseason spot.

On Thursday, McKee said the backup mindset is to be ready at a moment's notice so it's a positive that he will get practice time with the first team heading into his chance to make a strong impression on the Eagles and the entire league this Sunday.

"Every opportunity that you get to play is a huge opportunity, especially being a sixth-round pick," McKee said. "Every opportunity is a huge opportunity. I'm obviously very excited and ready to make the most of it."

The Eagles have a lot of injury issues beyond the one that's knocked Hurts out of action, so it's not an ideal situation for a backup to come in and shine but it's the chance that McKee gets and we'll see what he can do with it on Sunday.

item.title: Broncos won despite totaling just 32 yards on their last 10 possessions
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The Broncos' offense was stunningly bad for most of Thursday night's game.
item.content:encoded:
The Broncos' offense was stunningly bad for most of Thursday night's game. They beat the Seahawks anyway.

Over Denver's final 10 possessions — two in the second quarter, three in the third quarter, four in the fourth quarter and one in overtime — the Broncos' offense totaled 32 yards. Seven of those 10 possessions ended in punts, two ended with the ends of the first and second halves, and the one in overtime began in field goal range and ended with the game-winning field goal.

Broncos quarterback Bo Nix could not move the offense at all: He threw the ball 27 times for 107 yards, got sacked twice for a loss of 13 yards, and had four rushes for two yards. Add all that up, and in 33 plays, Nix totaled 96 yards. That's 2.9 yards per play. Usually, you can't win in the NFL when your quarterback is playing like that.

Fortunately for the Broncos, Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold also played a losing game. Darnold's overtime interception did something Nix couldn't: Put the Broncos in position to win.

(Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images)

item.title: Ryan Fitzpatrick on Bo Nix's night: "That right there is garbage"
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Quarterback-turned-analyst repeatedly tees off on Denver QB.
item.content:encoded:
The Broncos won on Thursday night, beating the defending Super Bowl champions in overtime. But the victory comes with a major asterisk; Denver's offense continues to be not good enough.

As Ryan Fitzpatrick of Prime Video put it after the game, quarterback Bo Nix is not good enough.

"Bo Nix is not playing competitively," Fitzpatrick said, growing increasingly animated as he went. "It's almost disrespectful to the quarterback position how he's playing quarterback right now. . . . He has no trust from his coach, he calls a screen play on third and eight. . . . Now they're in the locker room right now, they're excited. They won. He's not playing competitive football right now. . . . I can only imagine how Sean Payton feels. I mean, Sean Payton, [offensive coordinatpr] Davis Webb, everybody that blocks for him. He's not competing right now. And that's something that he's hung his hat on for the last two years. I don't know if he's still injured. I don't know what's going on. But it's not good enough. It's effort."

Later in the postgame show, Fitzpatrick was given another chance to elaborate on his critique of Nix.

“Well, there’s no fire and there’s no passion," Fitzpatrick said. "And that doesn’t mean you’ve got to be yelling at guys on the sideline or inspiring in the huddle. You can do it with your play as well. And I just don’t see it. And I just think that he needs to be sat down and they need to tell him being a quarterback in the NFL is a very special thing. And right now he’s taking it for granted. He is. And there’s a lot of guys that have played this game that watch that game that think, ‘That right there is garbage. That effort is garbage. That is not a quarterback in the NFL. We deserve better.’”

For the game, Nix completed 17 of 27 passes for 107 yards, no touchdowns, and no interceptions. His passer rating was 71.1. Denver's offense gained only 168 yards. Seattle gained 353.

It remains to be seen whether Payton will have anything to say publicly about Nix's play. Payton may have some pointed things to say privately — and if the issues continue, who knows what will happen?

Because Nix is in his third season, whatever comes next will be critical. Nix will be eligible for a second contract after the season.

And the Broncos' eventual options could be to either pay him market value or move on. Bot every team wants to kick the can or pay a mid-level contract to a guy who lands in the "average" category. To win consistently and to chase championships, it's critical to have a guy who's playing like a franchise quarterback.

item.title: New report links Greg Olsen to Monday Night Football in 2027
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The offseason game of broadcaster roulette will be intriguing, and expensive.
item.content:encoded:
The offseason game of broadcaster roulette will be intriguing, and expensive.

With the Monday Night Football spot at ESPN/ABC opening up if Troy Aikman leaves, there will be more than a few who want it. John Ourand of Puck drops a juicy nugget in the latest edition of The Varsity newsletter.

Take it away, John: "My best sources are predicting that Greg Olsen will wind up in ESPN’s Monday Night Football booth next season."

It's just a prediction, but Ourand wouldn't throw something like that around unless he had good reason to believe it.

Hovering over any of the top spots will be Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce, who has the chops and the cachet to pick his spot and name his price.

Olsen, who has won multiple Emmys (including the most recent one, from his spot on the Fox "B" team) seems destined to land with a No. 1 team, somewhere. Whether that's ESPN, CBS, or Prime Video, it seems inevitable that Olsen, who was bumped to the bench because Fox wanted Tom Brady, will once again have a prime spot, somewhere.

item.title: Seahawks need to consider whether Drew Lock gives them a better chance to win
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The conversation, however it's resolved, needs to be had.
item.content:encoded:
The conversation, however it's resolved, needs to be had.

Should the Seahawks turn to Drew Lock over Sam Darnold at quarterback?

Darnold has seven interceptions in four full games (he handled five snaps of the Week 1 game against the Patriots). Drew Lock threw four touchdown passes and no picks in most of the Patriots game and all of the Week 2 game against the Cardinals.

Darnold has started four games since returning from his glute injury. He's 1-3.

Said Darnold on Tuesday, regarding the miscues: "I’m going to continue to be as decisive as I can be and go through my reads and trust what I see, trust my feet, all those things. Can’t have turnovers. You have to protect the football in this league. If you don’t, you’ll pay.”

For a running back like James Cook of the Bills, a turnover problem could mean fewer reps and touches in the tailback rotation. For a quarterback, it's all or nothing; he either takes all the snaps, or he takes none of them.

At some point, the Seahawks need to ask themselves whether Lock should be the one taking the snaps.

Obviously, benching Darnold would likely mean the Seahawks would move on in 2027. His $35.5 million in compensation for next year, the last of his contract, isn't guaranteed. He earns a $10 million roster bonus on the fifth day of the league year in March.

The Seahawks may ultimately decide to ride or die with Darnold for the rest of the season. But they at least need to have the conversation about making a switch, and the possibility of being benched at some point needs to be on the table in order to underscore Darnold's assessment.

"You have to protect the football in this league. If you don’t, you’ll pay.”

item.title: Thursday Night Football: Broncos beat Seahawks 17-14 in overtime
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Wil Lutz kicked a 53-yard field goal with 4:53 remaining in overtime after Ja'Quan McMillian's pick of Sam Darnold.
item.content:encoded:
The Broncos had not lost a home game leading by 11 or more points in the fourth quarter since a 2004 loss to the Raiders. They still haven't.

The Seahawks rallied from 11 down in the fourth quarter to force overtime, but Sam Darnold threw an interception on the first possession of the extra period. Ja'Quan McMillian's pick at the Seattle 43 put the Broncos in field-goal range, and Wil Lutz kicked a 53-yard field goal to win it 17-14.

The Broncos moved to 4-2, while the Seahawks fell to 3-3.

In the second half, the Broncos had 30 yards and two first downs, going 0-for-6 on third down. Bo Nix was 7-of-12 for 29 yards in the final 30 minutes.

The Broncos gained only 8 yards on their game-winning, overtime field-goal drive, but it was enough.

The Seahawks couldn't get out of their own way all night: They had 91 yards and three points in the first half; Rashid Shaheed lost a fumble; Jason Myers missed a 47-yard field goal off the right upright in the third quarter; and Darnold threw two picks in crunch time.

The Seahawks were in field-goal range to tie the game late in the fourth quarter when Broncos cornerback Kris Abrams-Draine intercepted Darnold, undercutting Tory Horton at the Denver 31. The pick with 1:25 left didn't end the game as the Seahawks had all three timeouts.

The Broncos burned only 15 seconds off the clock before Shaheed returned Jeremy Crawshaw's punt 31 yards to the Seattle 46. Eight plays and 38 yards later, the game was tied on Myers 34-yard field goal with 3 seconds left in regulation.

The Seahawks had six drives inside the Denver 40 but had only a field goal, a touchdown and a 2-point conversion to show for it.

Seattle outgained Denver 353 to 168, with Darnold going 27-of-51 for 278 yards with two picks. He was pressured on 24 of his dropbacks, and the Broncos sacked him five times.

Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 12 passes for 134 yards after having only two catches for 11 yards at halftime.

Nix finished 17-of-27 for 107 yards, with RJ Harvey catching three passes for 31 yards. Harvey and J.K. Dobbins scored the Broncos' touchdowns on short runs.

item.title: NFL says it will be "selective" about playing on Wednesdays
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The NFL has begun scheduling some games on Wednesdays.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL has begun scheduling some games on Wednesdays. For now, "some" will be the operative word.

Via Drew Lerner of Awful Announcing, NFL executive V.P. and chief media officer Hans Schroeder said this week at a Front Office Sports event that Wednesday games are not likely to become the norm.

“We’re going to be selective,” Schroeder said. “I don’t think what you’re going to see is playing Wednesday football throughout the year. But if there’s opportunities to do something creative like we did on Wednesday and Thanksgiving Eve or like Christmas became on those certain days, we’re going to look at it. We’re going to figure out whether we think it’s a smart thing to do. And then we’re going to look at the numbers and make sure that the numbers and the viewership validates what our instincts are.”

While that explanation surely reflects the league's current thinking on the issue, the league's thinking about playing on Christmas once included no plan to play on Christmas when December 25 falls on a Tuesday or a Wednesday. Indeed, it was Schroeder who said that.

And then someone crunched the numbers and the owners said, "Do it."

That could happen with Wednesday night football. If Sunday Ticket is, as YouTube believes it will be, "deconstructed," the league would have an added incentive to peel more games from the Sunday afternoon cluster and drop them into prime-time windows.

Why not Wednesday night? Why not Tuesday night? The league learned during the pandemic that it's possible to pull it off, and with the league having no qualms about a Sunday-to-Thursday turnaround, it's possible to devise a schedule that has teams playing on the non-traditional days of the week.

For Wednesdays, the easiest approach would be to configure the schedule to give the assignment to teams emerging from a bye, or to teams who play on the prior Thursday. Tuesday night games could be the final contests of a given week, with the teams then playing on Sunday or Monday.

In the end, it will all be driven by the desire to make more and more money. And prime-time standalone games make more money than they do when dropped into a Sunday afternoon window with multiple other games.

item.title: Police continue to withhold the Josh Jacobs video
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: As Packers running back Josh Jacobs continues to spend the early weeks of the 2026 season on paid leave, the NFL reportedly still hasn't gotten access to the key piece of video generated by the incident that resulted in a no-contest plea to battery.
item.content:encoded:
As Packers running back Josh Jacobs continues to spend the early weeks of the 2026 season on paid leave, the NFL reportedly still hasn't gotten access to the key piece of video generated by the incident that resulted in a no-contest plea to battery.

Via Danielle Lerner of USA Today, police in Wisconsin are delaying the release of the video — both to the NFL and to the media.

Last month, the judge presiding over the criminal case lifted a temporary court order sealing the evidence in the case, while concluding that the Hobart-Lawrence Police Department had the discretion "to apply a balancing test between the rights of the public, the defendant and the victim in deciding whether to release the records."

In an October 13 letter to USA Today, Hobart-Lawrence police chief Michael Renkas explained that, although the department determined it could release some records with "appropriate redactions," it is required to wait because the lawyers in the underlying case intend to seek a new court order blocking the disclosure.

"Accordingly, the Department is temporarily withholding all responsive records in accordance with the statutory waiting period and any applicable court orders," Renkas wrote. "This temporary hold does not constitute a denial of your request or a reversal of the Department's balancing-test determination."

Some in league circles believe Jacobs could return from paid leave soon, with the games Jacobs has missed eventually being credited toward his suspension. However, it seems unlikely that the NFL will allow Jacobs to play until it sees the video.

The NFL learned the hard way the lesson of closing a player's Personal Conduct Policy case without first seeing the relevant video. The release of the Ray Rice elevator video in September 2014, coupled with a report that the NFL had seen it before it was leaked to TMZ, sparked a major controversy that threatened the employment of the Commissioner.

Surely, the league won't risk putting itself in that same position again. And so the bottom-line message is, or should be, that Jacobs doesn't play until the NFL sees the video.

item.title: Jets S Minkah Fitzpatrick will appeal fine for hit on Browns WR KC Concepcion
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Jets safety Minkah Fitzpatrick said he received a fine from the NFL for a hit that concussed Browns wide receiver KC Concepcion on Sunday.
item.content:encoded:
Jets safety Minkah Fitzpatrick said he received a fine from the NFL for a hit that concussed Browns wide receiver KC Concepcion on Sunday.

Fitzpatrick wouldn't reveal the fine amount but said he will appeal.

"It was a football play, in my opinion," Fitzpatrick said Thursday, via Antwan Staley of the New York Daily News. "Obviously, we don't like to see anybody get hurt. I'm happy to see that he's back out practicing this week. But in my opinion, it was a football play, a bang-bang play as their coach put it."

Fitzpatrick ripped off Concepcion's helmet, which also likely drew a fine from the league, in the first quarter before an unnecessary roughness penalty four plays later that knocked out Concepcion.

Concepcion returned to practice Wednesday but remains in concussion protocol after another limited practice Thursday.

“When you look at the league rules, they say you can’t hit a defenseless player,” Fitzpatrick said. “I really don’t know what that means.

“I understand why I got the penalty. It wasn’t for targeting or hitting him in the head. It was for hitting a defenseless player. In my opinion, when a receiver has the ball, you have every right to hit him as long as you are not hitting him in the head.”

Browns fans were not fans of Fitzpatrick before Sunday. They remember his tackle on then-Cleveland running back Nick Chubb in 2023 that tore ligaments and the meniscus in Chubb's left leg.

“I’m over that issue,” Fitzpatrick said of the Chubb play.

item.title: Troy Aikman: It seems like ESPN is going to go in a different direction
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Hall of Fame quarterback and ESPN/ABC Monday Night Football analyst Troy Aikman made some waves on Thursday morning by creating the clear impression that he's planning to leave after his current contract expires, after Super Bowl LXI.
item.content:encoded:
Hall of Fame quarterback and ESPN/ABC Monday Night Football analyst Troy Aikman made some waves on Thursday morning by creating the clear impression that he's planning to leave after his current contract expires, after Super Bowl LXI.

Aikman elaborated on his remarks to Jimmy Traina of Underscore Media.

"It just seems to be where they’re going — that they’re gonna go in a different direction because there’s been no talks, no contract negotiations," Aikman told Traina. "We’re in a Super Bowl year. The Super Bowl is Feb. 14. My contract ends in March. It just doesn’t seem logical that if they were gonna keep me, something wouldn’t be in place before that.”

The more recent quotes create a window for ESPN to still attempt to extend Aikman. He didn't say the door is closed from his perspective; he said he's sensing it's closed from the company's perspective. It officially won't close until his contract expires and he becomes a free agent.

Traina also asked Aikman whether he believes it will be difficult to finish the year, in light of his impression that ESPN won't be trying to keep him.

“The rest of the season will be fine," Aikman said. "Excited about it. Looking forward to it. It’s awesome that we got the Super Bowl. Not a problem at all."

In his latest comments, Aikman didn't address the report of tension with his long-time broadcast partner, Joe Buck, or the contention that they recently argued about the fact that Buck has signed a five-year extension while Aikman has been, by all appearances, frozen out.

Whether it's posturing from Aikman or not, all other potential suitors now know he's in play. Which will be a factor in the looming game of broadcaster musical chairs, with ESPN, CBS, and Prime Video all potentially looking to land one of the big names.

Aikman is among the biggest in football broadcasting. He's been part of a No. 1 team for a long time, and he could instantly move to top of the wish list for other networks that will be looking for a new lead NFL analyst.

item.title: Thursday Night Football: Broncos lead Seahawks 14-3 at halftime
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The Broncos have stymied the Seahawks, limiting them to 91 yards and forcing a fumble.
item.content:encoded:
The Broncos have a banged up secondary. It hasn't mattered.

Defensive coordinator Vance Joseph's unit forced three punts, recovered a fumble and allowed only a field goal. The Broncos lead 14-3 at halftime.

The Seahawks have 91 yards, including only 40 net passing yards, and are 2-for-6 on third down.

Sam Darnold is 7-of-15 for 52 yards and has been sacked twice. Jaxon Smith-Njigba has only two catches for 11 yards.

Sean Payton, who took over play-calling duties from offensive coordinator Davis Webb a game ago, has called a more balanced game with 17 runs and 15 passes, and the Broncos have 130 yards.

The Broncos had scored only 23 first-half points in their first five games combined.

Bo Nix is 10-of-15 for 78 yards, with running back RJ Harvey catching three for 31.

J.K. Dobbins has 11 carries for 35 yards.

The Seahawks lost tight end Elijah Arroyo, who injured his shoulder while trying to recover Rashid Shaheed's fumble. He is doubtful to return. The Broncos have ruled out running back Tyler Badie with a left thumb injury.

item.content:encoded:
The Broncos entered Thursday night ranked 30th in total offense, including 25th in rushing. They are having no problem moving the ball against the league's No. 1 defense, though.

The Broncos have 125 yards, including 51 rushing, after three drives against the Seahawks.

RJ Harvey's 1-yard touchdown run with 5:15 remaining in the first half has the Broncos holding a 14-3 lead.

Seahawks cornerback Devon Witherspoon was called for a 20-yard defensive pass interference penalty on Courtland Sutton in the end zone to set up Harvey's score.

J.K. Dobbins scored the team's first touchdown on a 4-yard run.

Dobbins has 10 carries for 35 yards and Harvey three carries for 10 yards.

Bo Nix is 9-of-13 for 74 yards.

item.title: Jon Morris, a member of the Patriots Hall of Fame, died at 84
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Jon Morris, a member of the Patriots Hall of Fame, has died, the team announced Thursday.
item.content:encoded:
Jon Morris, a member of the Patriots Hall of Fame, has died, the team announced Thursday. He was 84.

The cause of death was undisclosed.

The Boston Patriots selected Morris in the fourth round in the 1964 AFL draft, and the Packers took him in the second round of the NFL draft. The Holy Cross product signed with the Patriots and spent 11 of his 15 NFL seasons in New England.

Morris was a six-time AFL all-star center from 1964-69 and a Pro Bowl selection in 1970 when the team joined the NFL as part of the AFL-NFL merger.

Morris spent the 1974-77 seasons in Detroit before a final season with Chicago in 1978.

“Jon Morris was one of the great players who helped build the foundation of our franchise,” Patriots owner Robert Kraft said in a statement. “For generations of Patriots fans, he represented the toughness, dedication and pride of those early teams.”

Morris played alongside future Patriots Hall of Famers Gino Cappelletti, Babe Parilli and Jim Nance, and he went into the team's Hall of Fame in 2011. Morris was also included on the Patriots’ 50th anniversary team in 2009.

item.title: Caleb Williams confirms he tore his hamstring, doesn't know his status for Sunday
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Williams has had two full practices this week as he works his way back from the Week 2 injury.
item.content:encoded:
Caleb Williams has had two full practices this week, but the Bears quarterback insists he doesn't know whether he will return for Sunday's game against the Falcons.

“Before you start asking, I do not know if I’m playing yet,” Williams said Thursday, via Dan Wiederer of TheAthletic.com.

Williams injured his hamstring in a Sept. 20 game, and he has missed the past three games. He said he has checkpoints to clear and a "stress test" to pass before he can play.

In his first media availability since his injury, Williams explained what happened when he went down awkwardly on a red-zone scramble in the fourth quarter of the 9-3 loss to the Vikings.

“I felt a pop,” Williams said. “That’s why I looked back. I looked back just like everybody else does when you feel a pop. [You] think somebody grabbed you, and nobody grabbed me.”

Williams took issue with reports that he was diagnosed with a strain, which some labeled a Grade 2 strain.

“It was a hamstring tear,” Williams said, “and a pretty serious one.”

Williams would not reveal the grade tear he has.

“We got a grade, but I wouldn’t say it’s deserved to be put out there after all the false [reports],” Williams said. “So next question.”

item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Cowboys cornerback Joey Porter Jr. participated fully in Thursday's practice, and he expects to have no limitations for Sunday's game against the Packers.
item.content:encoded:
Cowboys cornerback Joey Porter Jr. participated fully in Thursday's practice, and he expects to have no limitations for Sunday's game against the Packers.

"That's what I’m shooting for. That's what they're shooting for as well," Porter told Patrik Walker of the team website. "So that's what we're gonna try to do."

Porter was inactive at the start of the season with the Steelers after not getting the expected long-term contract extension. He played 25 snaps in his debut with the Cowboys in Week 4, but missed the Week 5 game last Thursday night after coming down with an illness on game day.

"I really just couldn't hold anything down," Porter told Walker. "You know, I just kept throwing up. I try to fight through. I tried to take a nap before the game, just to shake it off, but I just couldn't hold in deep down. So that's when they made the call to send me home."

Porter was limited in Wednesday's practice with an ankle injury that he injured during the Cowboys' victory over the Texans in Week 4.

Linebacker DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring) and cornerback Ameer Speed (knee) returned to limited work in Thursday's practice after sitting out Wednesday. Outside linebacker Von Miller was the only other change to the injury report, returning to a full practice after a rest day.

Cornerback Cobie Durant (hamstring) and offensive tackle Drew Shelton (hamstring) remained out of practice.

Safety Alijah Clark (hamstring), outside linebacker James Houston (shoulder), cornerback Shavon Revel Jr. (knee) and left guard Tyler Smith (thumb) were again full participants.

item.title: Cowboys DC Christian Parker: Mike Pettine a "right-hand man" not a "save the day" hire
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Cowboys hired longtime NFL defensive coordinator and former Browns head coach Mike Pettine as a senior defensive assistant this week and defensive coordinator Christian Parker was asked at a Thursday press conference if Pettine is a "save the day" hire after a rough start.
item.content:encoded:
The Cowboys hired longtime NFL defensive coordinator and former Browns head coach Mike Pettine as a senior defensive assistant this week and defensive coordinator Christian Parker was asked at a Thursday press conference if Pettine is a "save the day" hire after a rough start.

Parker said, via Clarence Hill of DLLS Sports, that "I don’t need to respond to that" and explained that he sees Pettine as a "right-hand man" in his first season running the defense. Parker's first NFL job was working under Pettine in Green Bay in 2019 and Parker outlined how he plans to utilize the veteran coach for the rest of this year.

"Sounding board, advancing, watching film, he'll have an area of expertise just like all the position coaches do," Parker said, via the team's website. "I think when we come in Monday, he's already kind of gotten ahead on the next opponent, those kinds of things. Those roles usually are focused on advances, some area of expertise, and just kind of having a guy to bounce ideas off of."

Parker said that he views the Cowboys' defensive problems as "very fixable" and Sunday night against the Packers would be an ideal time to show that the staff has started that process.
